title: 40 Years of Evolution: Darwin's Finches on Daphne Major Island
author: Peter R. Grant; B. Rosemary Grant
note: Selected with moderate confidence: strong specialist reception and a favorable but small Goodreads sample (4.15/27). The American Biology Teacher's detailed review recommends the revised book; Tim Birkhead's endorsement of the original is reproduced in Princeton's catalog. This is a sustained explanation of a longitudinal discovery program, not a technical curriculum or field reference. Statistical detail does not require completing a course to understand the main discoveries. Ecological mechanisms dominate, so T11=-10; no political or philosophical thematic deduction. No serious veto established from inspected evidence. Original publication remains 2014 despite the updated purchase edition.
notes: Longitudinal measurements and explicit data support claims; observational inference and generalization beyond one island remain bounded.
Integrates heredity, behavior, ecological constraints and population change rather than technology or institutions.
Long observation, rare events and changing selection pressures give transferable lessons for inference.
Strong explanation of competition, hybridization and changing trait distributions.
